lesson.topicTitle: 1. Structure, Bonding & Introduction to Organic Chemistry

specAnchors.text: understand the concepts of homologous series and functional group

primer.text: Organic chemistry runs on families: a homologous series shares one functional group and climbs by CH2 steps, its chemistry constant while boiling points and densities drift upward. The functional group is the property engine, and R - any group except hydrogen - generalises it across skeletons. This note defines the series and reads the groups table.

modules.title: Families that grow by CH2
modules.opening: A homologous series is organic chemistry's family tree: compounds sharing one functional group, each successive member one CH2 longer than the last. Members share a general formula and near-identical chemistry, while their physical properties - boiling point, melting point, density - slide gradually as the molecules grow. Ethanol to propanol is exactly one CH2 step; the alkane series is the classic ladder.
keyPoints: Members of a homologous series all carry the same functional group.
Each successive member differs by a CH2 unit.
Every member shares the same general formula and similar chemical properties.
Physical properties - boiling point, melting point, density - change gradually along the series.
Ascending the series enlarges the molecules, shifting those physical properties.

low.restatement: Same reactive group, same formula pattern, one CH2 per rung: the family climbs a ladder of ever-so-slightly heavier molecules.
low.analogy: One house design (functional group) built on plots of growing size: same layout, steadily larger garden each step.
low.examPointer: The CH2 increment is the definitional phrase - quote 'successive members differ by CH2' verbatim.

medium.restatement: The series is defined chemically (shared functional group and general formula) and graded physically: each CH2 addition raises molecular size, so dispersion-driven properties like boiling point and density climb gradually while reactivity stays put.
medium.analogy: A staircase where every step is the same height (CH2) but the view (physical properties) changes slowly with altitude.
medium.examPointer: Distinguish the invariants (functional group, general formula, chemical properties) from the sliders (boiling point, melting point, density).

modules.title: Functional groups run the show
sourceHeadings: Functional Groups Found in Compounds Table
modules.opening: The functional group is the business end of an organic molecule: the atom or group that determines its physical and chemical properties. In the common-groups table, R is the placeholder for whatever other atom or atom-cluster the molecule carries, hydrogen excepted - one group pattern, a whole family of compounds.
keyPoints: Physical behaviour and chemical reactivity both flow from the functional group.
The common functional groups are summarised in a reference table.
R is the stand-in for any other atom or atom-group - hydrogen excluded.
Identifying the functional group identifies the reactive behaviour of the compound.
The same group pattern in different molecules places them in the same homologous series.

low.restatement: Find the functional group and you have found the molecule's personality: how it reacts and much of how it behaves.
low.analogy: The engine in a car: body and colour vary (the R group), but the engine decides how it drives.
low.examPointer: Remember R's restriction: any atom or group EXCEPT hydrogen - hydrogen gets its own explicit slot in the tables.

medium.restatement: Functional groups are the reactive determinants of organic chemistry: the group's bonding pattern fixes both the chemical reactions available and the physical behaviour of the class, while R generalises the pattern across every carbon skeleton except bare hydrogen.
medium.analogy: A USB port standardises what any device can do regardless of its housing - the group defines the interface, R is the housing.
medium.examPointer: When asked to identify a series or predict reactions, point at the functional group first and the R group second.

glossary.definition: A family of organic compounds sharing a functional group, whose successive members differ by CH2.
The atom or group of atoms that determines a molecule's physical and chemical properties.
The formula pattern shared by every member of a homologous series.
